subject: Stratify: token-pressure and safety-lane plan for committed Dedicated deployment
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@stratify.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production traffic profile + committed terms

Hi Jonas / Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement asked for a concrete sizing recommendation for the Dedicated deployment that maps to our proposed commit. High-level numbers from our telemetry:
- Monthly committed tokens: 1.2 billion
- Typical request length (prompt + completion): 420 tokens median, 95th percentile 1,200 tokens
- Observed concurrency pattern: sustained window ~3k tokens/sec during business hours, short bursts up to ~18k tokens/sec (1–3 minute spikes, ~2–3x more frequent around new feature releases)
- Peak request size distribution skews heavy (a small % of requests are long generations)

Attached is a CSV with per-hour historic token counts for the last 30 days (stratify_qps_profile.csv). Can you provide a recommended slab layout (GPU SKUs, slabs, and recommended safety buffer) and confirm whether the committed level maps to the SLA targets we discussed (p95 tail latency <= 600ms for chat flows)?

Also looping in procurement depending on what the costing/commit tiers look like.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform, Stratify
elena@stratify.ai

P.S. We can redact any customer IDs if needed for the attachment.

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena@stratify.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production traffic profile + committed terms

Elena — thanks for the data. I pulled the CSV and ran a quick throughput model with Soojin to map tokens/sec to GPU slabs. Summary up front:

- Baseline mapping (model: open-nt-large, mixed precision FP16 + int8 quantized path):
  - Sustained 3,000 tokens/sec maps to ~0.9 of a single H100 slab (we define a slab as 8x H100 configured for inference).
  - Burst headroom to 18,000 tokens/sec requires ~2.6 slabs total; to keep latency SLOs we recommend reserving 3 slabs (safety buffer ~15%).
- Latency fit: with continuous batching and KV cache warm, p95 chat flows ~= 420–520ms on 3 slabs under the observed burst profile; long generations (1,200 tokens) push p95 toward 700–850ms if we don’t pre-warm cache — recommended mitigation: plan for autoscale warm-up policy and a per-route micro-cache for heavy gen flows.
- Safety and commit sizing: for a committed 1.2B tokens/month we recommend a 3-slab Reserved pool with configurable burst credit. That maps to an operational cap of ~75M tokens/day sustainable with the recommended safety lane for the expected request mix.

Attached: stratify_dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx (sheet with per-hour headroom sims and GPU utilization curves). High-level cost impact: 3 slabs (reserved) vs 2 slabs (reserved + on-demand burst) is a ~22% delta in monthly commitment.

Next steps: Soojin, can you add a row for an alternate configuration using 6x A100 (80GB) slabs (cost/perf trade) and one using more aggressive int8 quantization (estimated +1.6x throughput)? Elena — let us know whether procurement prefers a lower committed slab count with predictable burst credits or a higher reserved floor with cheaper per-token economics.

cheers,
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

---
Attachment note: I removed customer PII from the CSV.

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production traffic profile + committed terms (A100 / int8 variants)

Quick internal note (cc Ben for pricing):

- A100 80GB layout: 6x A100 slab (slab = 8x A100) gives similar memory headroom for long generations but lower sustained tokens/sec per slab vs H100 (~0.85x). For Stratify mix that means: sustained 3k t/s -> ~1.05 slabs; bursts to 18k t/s -> ~3.2 slabs. Operational recommendation: 4 slabs reserved (A100) + 1 slab burst/firebreak = similar latency band but ~8% higher monthly cost on our current pricing.
- int8 quantization (aggressive): we ran a conservative estimate — int8 path yields ~1.6x throughput improvement for typical prompt shapes but increases variance on p95 for the long-tail generations. If we assume int8 + H100, the 3-slab recommendation drops to 2 slabs reserved + 1 burst slab (effectively lower commit). Risk: potential small regression on generation quality for some proprietary tokens (we should run evals with Stratify prompt set).

Attached: short model-run logs and quality note (included in sizing workbook). Action items:
1) Ben to include pricing for: (a) 3x H100 reserved, (b) 4x A100 reserved, (c) 2x H100 reserved + burst credits with int8.
2) Jonas to draft a short SLA appendix that calls out p95 latency band and burst-handling policy (canary for new releases).

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Inference Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena@stratify.ai>, procurement@stratify.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production traffic profile + committed terms — proposal and next steps

Elena / Stratify procurement —

Thanks for the profile. Attached is a short commercial summary and a draft SLA appendix (redwood_draft_sla_terms.pdf) that matches the 3-slab H100 reserved configuration with the burst credit policy we discussed. Pricing options enclosed in the workbook:
- Option A (recommended): 3x H100 reserved slabs, 15% safety buffer, burst credits (auto-burst to on-demand) — best per-token economics and meets p95 <= 600ms for chat with recommended cache warm policy.
- Option B: 4x A100 reserved (higher monthly commit, slightly more conservative for long generations).
- Option C: 2x H100 reserved + aggressive int8 burst (lower commit, requires evals for quality acceptance; mitigations documented).

Please review and tell us which option procurement prefers; if Option C is attractive we will schedule a short eval run (48–72 hours) on your key prompt set. Also happy to jump on a call to walk through the amortized token math.
